messages.subject: [OGRUG] Quick Survey Until 11 April 2013: Towards a Training Course in Free/Libre/Open Source Licensing and Contracting
messages.subject_clean: [OGRUG] Quick Survey Until 11 April 2013: Towards a Training Course in Free/Libre/Open Source Licensing and Contracting
messages.body_plain:
OGRUG colleagues, Recently I've been contracted by a global firm which is
very active in the free/libre/open source world, to develop a course on
minimizing business risk and maximizing business value through
free/libre/open source licensing and contracting. While the topic itself is
tangenial to this list, nevertheless I've long considered the R community
to be amongst the most effective free/libre/open communities. I refer to it
fairly often as providing something close to an archetype for distributed
free/libre/open quality control methodology.

My client agrees that the generic contents of the training course we are
creating should itself be dual-licensed under the GNU-FDL and CC-BY
licenses.

Responses to this short questionnaire will help us to ensure that the
generic course meets the needs and preferences of diverse teams and
individual professionals. This requires 5-to-10 minutes to complete.

http://freeonlinesurveys.com/s.asp?sid=6pjtq7tro6rrq8y239996
(Note: Some have reported *asterisks* showing up on each end of this URL on
the receiving end. Please take the URL without them.)

Please suggest improvements to the scope of this work, directly within the
questionnaire. Report any glitches or typos directly to my email.

The results of this survey will be shared back with recipients (minus the
list of respondent names and emails) from this location:
http://www.projectmanagementhotel.com/projects/optimization-free-libre-open

We'll be grateful for any collaboration. Please forward to individuals you
think would have a direct interest in this.

-- 
Joseph Potvin
Operations Manager | Gestionnaire des operations
The Opman Company | La compagnie Opman
http://www.projectmanagementhotel.com/projects/opman-portfolio
jpotvin at opman.ca <http://--esfsecev------/>

At the meetup there was some interest in some work I'd done to present 
Sweave, KnitR and odfWeave, as well as Latex -> Epub.

I've put the slides on my server at

http://macnash.telfer.uottawa.ca/~nashjc/visible/

nash-oclug130307.odp -- lightning talk about Latex -> epub.

UOpsych130311.odp -- latest version of a talk about updateable reports 
(including graphics) using Sweave, KnitR or odfWeave.

Best,

John Nash

messages.subject: [OGRUG] Big honk'n spreadsheet error
messages.body_plain:
More...  A colleague mentions: "this circulated on R-help yesterday. The
blog  actually has details of the error. They are saying it does not change
the conclusion, but it is pretty sad. It at least says a lot about
providing enough for others to check your work."
 _______________

Date: Wed, 17 Apr 2013 09:16:15 -0400
From: Gabor Grothendieck <ggrothendieck at gmail.com>
To: Sarah Goslee <sarah.goslee at gmail.com>
Cc: r-help <r-help at r-project.org>
Subject: Re: [R] the joy of spreadsheets (off-topic)
Message-ID:
    <CAP01uRnBeo4NV86H_O6fcqMViK8LsNb3xiMqYe54-2x-WpxrZw at mail.gmail.com>
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=ISO-8859-1

On Tue, Apr 16, 2013 at 1:25 PM, Sarah Goslee <sarah.goslee at gmail.com>
wrote:
> Given that we occasionally run into problems with comparing Excel
> results to R results, and other spreadsheet-induced errors, I thought
> this might be of interest.
>
>
http://www.nextnewdeal.net/rortybomb/researchers-finally-replicated-reinhart-rogoff-and-there-are-serious-problems
>
> The punchline:
>
> "If this error turns out to be an actual mistake Reinhart-Rogoff made,
> well, all I can hope is that future historians note that one of the
> core empirical points providing the intellectual foundation for the
> global move to austerity in the early 2010s was based on someone
> accidentally not updating a row formula in Excel."
>
> Ouch.
>
> (Note: I know nothing about the site, the author of the article, or
> the study in question. I was pointed to it by someone else. But if
> true: highly problematic.)
>

Herndon, Ash and Pollin (HAP), the authors of the critique, found that
in the highest debt category the Excel error in Rienhart and Rogoff
(RR)  was -0.3 percent points compared to a total error (from that
plus RR's other 2 mistakes) of -2.3 percentage points.  See Figure 1
of HAP. Thus aside from the dubiousness of attributing the coding
error in Excel to Excel itself it was not the main source of the
discrepancy.

Also even if one backs out all three errors that they found, the key
conclusion that GDP growth is declining with debt still occurs (but to
a lesser extent) as pointed out by RR in an initial responding email
reported by Bloomberg News.

The key takeaway here is really unrelated to Excel but rather is that
until data and analyses are shared or made public so that the analysis
can be reproduced one cannot have any real confidence in research
results.

RR
http://www.nber.org/papers/w15639.pdf

HAP
http://www.peri.umass.edu/fileadmin/pdf/working_papers/working_papers_301-350/WP322.pdf

Bloomberg News
http://www.bloomberg.com/news/2013-04-16/reinhart-rogoff-paper-cited-by-ryan-faulted-for-serious-errors-.html

--

GKX Group, GKX Associates Inc.

email: ggrothendieck at gmail.com
